searchText: yep, when there's a fork you would change the fork version in the state (setting the prev to the current and the current to the new one) along with whatever other changes you want to make i ve noticed this `https://github.com/wealdtech/go-eth2-types/blob/master/domain.go#L21` while trolling through <@!144468805697929216> s code , mentioning that there are no fork requirements for a deposit? is that the case? <@!425279588009246720> Spec at https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/validator.md#submit-deposit states that the deposit must be signed with `GENESIS_FORK_VERSOIN` wrong alex 😛 thanks jim Oops sorry axic (when you show up) has a multiplier to the validator returns been considered until phase 1 or 2? Granted less people will stake while it's riskier (unproven tech & they will have their funds locked until the later phases) and the returns will be higher, but perhaps there could be an additional multiplier (say... `x1.2`) which goes away the minute people can withdraw their funds. Or perhaps such extra level of incentivization is unnecessary and the curve should do it's job Compiled my notes on the fork issue above here: https://hackmd.prylabs.network/s/BJ6-wdFHw Looking for feedback from anyone

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: yep, when there's a fork you would change the fork version in the state (setting the prev to the current and the current to the new one)
